text.title: Spec Example: Ecommerce Cart Core Rules
text.summary: Testable rules grounding Spec Example: Ecommerce Cart, including the five adaptation rules embedded in the full spec (personas, NFR sources, out-of-scope timing, preliminary data model, open questions). Each pairs a binary check with a sourced rationale; HARD rules — user-supplied input cannot override.

rule.statement: Example is fully filled in — no placeholders, no placeholders anywhere in the example body.
Authors who adapt the example record archetype = 'ecommerce-cart' in front-matter.
Example version matches spec-structure version; updates ship in the same PR.
Every section in the adapted spec is either rewritten OR explicitly marked 'kept from example'.
rule.rationale: Verbatim copies signal lack of engagement.

rule.statement: Example covers a single-team well-bounded feature; multi-team scope is excluded.
rule.rationale: Wider scope belongs in spec-advanced-guidelines example.

rule.statement: Example AC are all testable binary checks; vague AC removed.
rule.rationale: Setting the bar in the example forces the bar in adapted specs.

rule.statement: Define at least two personas with distinct goals and pain points; single-persona specs miss edge cases.
rule.rationale: Sarah drives the "quick add" UX; Mike drives the "persistence across sessions" requirement. Different personas justify different acceptance criteria that would otherwise look redundant.

rule.statement: Mark every NFR target with [SOURCE REQUIRED] when adapting this example; never copy numeric targets without a real measurement basis.
rule.rationale: NFR values without measurement sources survive unchanged into design and implementation. The 200ms / 50k figures are plausible for a mid-scale platform but have no basis in any specific project.

rule.statement: Include a "When" column in Out of Scope; "Not now" without a timeline reappears as scope creep in the next sprint.
rule.rationale: The "Out of Scope / When" column is the highest-ROI section for preventing feature creep mid-sprint. Copy this pattern into every spec.

rule.statement: Mark all data models in a spec as "preliminary — subject to change in design.md".
rule.rationale: Agents treat TypeScript interfaces in spec Appendix as canonical data models. The spec model is intent only; the approved model lives in design.md after architectural decisions are made.

rule.statement: Include an Open Questions section in every spec; if there are no questions, either the spec is complete or the author didn't look hard enough.
rule.rationale: Open questions are forcing functions: unanswered, they become assumptions in design.md. Documented, they become explicit review targets before approval.

rule.statement: If preconditions in AGENTS.md "Applies If" do not all hold, OR any "Skip If" disqualifier is true, do not run this methodology — route to the named alternative.
rule.rationale: Methodologies are pre-condition gated; running them out-of-scope produces noise and burns the agent context budget.

rule.statement: If preconditions hold, execute the procedure in `content/04-procedure.xml` (or the rule set above when complexity is light), emit the artefact specified by `content/02-output-contract.xml`, and validate with `scripts/validate-spec-example-ecommerce-cart.py` before returning.
rule.rationale: Tying the entry rule to the validator script closes the loop between policy and machine check.
